# CentralDogma Package

Tools for working with the central dogma of molecular biology, from DNA to RNA to protein. The package provides functions for splitting a DNA sequence into codons in a chosen reading frame, which is the first step in translating a coding sequence into its amino acid sequence. It also provides a plot of Amino Acid frequency, which makes it easy to view the composition of the sequnence.

# Function 2

# Function 3 - getCodon Function

Split a DNA sequence into codons

Takes a single DNA sequence and cuts it into consecutive, non-overlapping three-letter codons. The \`start\` argument sets the reading frame (1, 2 or 3), so reading can begin at any of the first three bases. Any leftover bases at the end that cannot form a full codon are dropped. The result is a character vector with one codon per element, ready for use in translation to amino acids

# Function 4

# Function 5 - Amino Acid Frequency Plot

Creates a bar plot showing the frequency of amino acids in a protein sequence. Takes a single protein sequence as input, identifies each unique amino acid present, and counts how many times it occurs within the sequence. These counts are organised into a data frame and visualised as a ggplot2 bar chart, where each bar represents the frequency of a particular amino acid. The function returns the completed ggplot object, allowing it to be displayed or further customised by the user.
